deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 16% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.0% = 10-year Treasury 5.0% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 15% last year; 8%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 97% (3 years ago 87%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $97 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 118% (3 years ago 156%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $14.8B, up 8% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Inventory up 154% vs quarterly sales up 12% (days of inventory 10 → 22). Products may be building up unsold — a warning sign in chip cycles.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 8%/yr over 3 years and 6%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 33% vs a 5-year range of 29–33% (median 31%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $102.1B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($86.4B buybacks + $15.7B dividends) = 2.0% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.6% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $10.57, down 1% in 90 days (down 2% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 10 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $9.41, down 1% in 90 days (down 2% in the last 30); 7 analysts raised, 23 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest year vs a year earlier: Americas 41% of sales, up 11%; Europe 27% of sales, up 15%; Greater China 17% of sales, up 28%; Rest of Asia Pacific 8% of sales, up 18%; 1 smaller. Source: 10-K XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $97.5M, 100% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

note.headline: Apple's cash machine keeps growing, but 354.88 still sits above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is a high-quality, cash-rich business with rising margins, but at 354.88 the price already assumes much faster cash-flow growth than the company has delivered, and analysts are trimming next year's profit estimates.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. Nothing in the data justifies paying today's price, and no clean trade setup shows up in the levels.
summary.act_at: Long-term near 313.15 or lower; swing only after a pullback toward 348.15–351.73 that holds

note.happening: Apple closed at 354.88, down 0.21% on the day. It is still moving sideways in a range, inside a price zone of 354.33–356.43, above its 50-day average of 338.48 and its 200-day average of 300.51. There is no new news since yesterday. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-28.
note.business: Some facts change the business itself. The latest quarter, filed 2026-11-03, was strong. Twelve-month revenue reached 478.8B, up from 416.2B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. Operating margin improved to 33.01% from 31.97%. Growth is slowing, though: quarterly sales growth was 11.72%, down from 16.6% two quarters ago. The clearest business risk is inventory, which is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%. If that product does not sell, Apple may have to cut prices, and margins would suffer. Other facts mostly touch sentiment or governance. The annual report added a risk factor about an investigation, and the data does not say whether it will cost money. Cash and survival are not at risk: liquidity is 56.7B and yearly free cash flow is 136.1B, far larger than the net debt of 23.4B. What is at risk is margins and the growth rate the stock price depends on. Segment data is not available, so we cannot see which product lines are driving these trends.

worth.text: Every valuation method lands below today's price. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 146.14 in the bear case, 226.4 in the base case and 313.15 in the bull case. Apple's own price-to-sales history gives 222.27–300.79. The main assumption behind the gap is how fast free cash flow grows at the start. To justify 354.88, cash flow would need to start growing at about 26.7% a year. The 3-year sales growth rate is 7.7% and last year's was 15%. At 20% starting growth the model gives 274.92, and only at 30% does it reach 402.47. The stock trades at 39.5 times trailing earnings and 33.5 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio of 10.8 is about twice the peer median of 5.5 and at the top of Apple's own 5-year range. Margins matter too: if operating margin fell to 24%, the model value drops to 205.79.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free cash flow growth: the price implies about 26.7%, while the 3-year sales growth rate is 7.7% and last year's was 15%.

bull: Free cash flow jumped to 136.1B from 98.8B a year earlier, and operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%.
Apple is shrinking its share count, down 1.56% over the year, so each share owns more of the profits.
Analysts raised this year's EPS estimate by 6.4% over the last 30 days, to 9.4.
bear: Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, which is a risk to prices and margins.
Next-year EPS estimates were cut 2.3% in 30 days (10.83 to 10.58), and next quarter's were cut 3.7%.
Price-to-sales of 10.8 sits at the 100th percentile of Apple's own 5-year range and well above the peer median of 5.5.

levels.what: Today's close, above the top of every valuation range, so there is little room for disappointment.
The DCF bull-case value and the top of the fair-value range. Below this, the price would sit inside the range.
The high end of Apple's own price-to-sales history, and close to the 200-day average of 300.51.

longterm.why: This is a grade-B business with growing cash flow. But the price needs cash-flow growth near 26.7%, and analysts are cutting next year's estimates.

swing.why: The stock is in a sideways range with a flat 20-day average, and the data shows no resistance level to use as a target. The nearest support zones are 348.15–351.73 and 342.99–345.34. Without a target, there is no way to build a risk-to-reward plan.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-28 report is the next big test of inventory and slowing growth. January options (expiring 2027-01-15, before earnings) price a 7.8% move, and falling estimates argue against acting before the report.

change_mind: The price drops to 313.15 or lower while free cash flow stays near 136.1B. That would put the stock inside the fair-value range.
Next-year EPS estimates turn back up above 10.83, where they stood 30 days ago, which would reverse the current cuts.
The 2027-01-28 report shows inventory growth moving back in line with sales growth of about 12%, while operating margin holds near 33.01%. A slide toward 24% would cut the model value to 205.79.
note.what_changed: The price slipped to 354.88 from 355.63 with no new news, and the support zones were redrawn lower to 348.15–351.73. The view is unchanged because the valuation gap and the estimate cuts are the same.
